question.problem:
Suppose we wish to find a zero of the function $f(x,y)$ in the region $[0,3]\times [-2,2]⊆{R}^{2},$ where $$ f(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}-xy-4 \\ x-{y}^{3}-1\end{aligned}]. $$ Calculate the second iteration of the Newton-Raphson process that starts at ${x}_{0}=[2,\,0]^{T}$ if the first iteration of the algorithm gives ${x}_{1}=[1,\,-2]^{T}.$ Round your final answer to three decimal places (if needed).
${x}_{2}≈[$ {{field-1}} $]$
{{field-2}}
question.worked_solution:
The Newton-Raphson method of finding the zeros of a multivariable function $f:{R}^{n}\to {R}^{n}$ is

$$
{x}_{n+1}={x}_{n}-[{J}_{f}({x}_{n})]^{-1}f({x}_{n}),
$$

where ${J}_{f}({x}_{n})$ is the Jacobian of $f$ evaluated at ${x}_{n}.$

In our case, the Jacobian is

$$
\begin{aligned}{J}_{f}(x) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}-xy-4) & \frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{2}-xy-4) \\ \frac{∂}{∂x}(x-{y}^{3}-1) & \frac{∂}{∂y}(x-{y}^{3}-1)\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2x-y & -x \\ 1 & -3{y}^{2}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our Newton-Raphson formula is

$$
{x}_{n+1}={x}_{n}-{[\begin{aligned}2x-y & -x \\ 1 & -3{y}^{2}\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{n}}^{-1}{[\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}-xy-4 \\ x-{y}^{3}-1\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{n}}.
$$

For the second iteration, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{2} & ={x}_{1}-{[\begin{aligned}2x-y & -x \\ 1 & -3{y}^{2}\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{1}}^{-1}{[\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}-xy-4 \\ x-{y}^{3}-1\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{1}} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2\end{aligned}]-{[\begin{aligned}2(1)-(-2) & -1 \\ 1 & -3(-2)^{2}\end{aligned}]}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}{1}^{2}-(1)(-2)-4 \\ 1-(-2)^{3}-1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2\end{aligned}]-{[\begin{aligned}4 & -1 \\ 1 & -12\end{aligned}]}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 8\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2\end{aligned}]-\frac{1}{4\cdot (-12)-(-1)\cdot 1}[\begin{aligned}-12 & 1 \\ -1 & 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 8\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2\end{aligned}]+\frac{1}{47}[\begin{aligned}20 \\ 33\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{67}{47} \\ -\frac{61}{47}\end{aligned}] \\  & ≈[\begin{aligned}1.426 \\ -1.298\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to three decimal places.
